text: ἥλιον ὑμνεῖν αὖτε Διὸς τέκος ἄρχεο Μοῦσα
meaning: "And now, O Muse Calliope, daughter of Zeus, begin to sing of glowing Helios." The opening of the Homeric Hymn to Helios, the Sun.
purpose: To greet the Sun and the strength of a new day.
note: Sunday is the Sun’s day across Greek, Roman, Norse (Sunna), Indian (Surya) and Japanese reckoning. Translation: Hugh G. Evelyn-White, 1914 (public domain).
source: Homeric Hymn 31, To Helios, line 1 (Perseus); translation Hugh G. Evelyn-White, 1914
name: Hymn to Helios
iast: hḗlion humneîn aûte Diòs tékos árkheo Moûsa
pronunciation: HAY-lee-on hoom-NAYN OW-te dee-OS TE-kos AR-khe-o MOO-sa
